questions.question: What Google metric measures page experience?
questions.explanation: Core Web Vitals assess loading, interactivity, and stability.

questions.question: What technique builds topic authority?
questions.explanation: Topic clusters organize related content.

questions.question: What markup helps search engines display rich results?
questions.explanation: Schema.org vocabulary enhances search listings.

questions.question: What algorithm update penalizes low-quality content?
questions.explanation: Panda targets thin or duplicate content.

questions.question: What algorithm targets unnatural backlinks?
questions.explanation: Penguin penalizes manipulative link schemes.

questions.question: What measures content indexability?
questions.explanation: Crawl budget limits pages crawled per site.

questions.question: What technique improves JavaScript SEO?
questions.explanation: SSR makes JavaScript content crawlable.

questions.question: What identifies search intent categories?
questions.explanation: Intent classifies informational, navigational, or transactional searches.

questions.question: What link attribute prevents authority transfer?
questions.explanation: nofollow tells crawlers not to follow links.

questions.question: What measures page relevance through links?
questions.explanation: PageRank evaluates link-based authority.

questions.question: What Google NLP model interprets conversational query context?
questions.explanation: BERT understands natural language in searches.

questions.question: What HTTP header controls indexing for non-HTML resources like PDFs?
questions.explanation: X-Robots-Tag applies robots directives via headers.

questions.question: What Google machine-learning system interprets never-before-seen queries?
questions.explanation: RankBrain maps novel queries to relevant results.

questions.question: What attribute signals localized page versions for different languages or regions?
questions.explanation: hreflang serves correct regional page variants.

questions.question: What informal term describes authority passed through hyperlinks?
questions.explanation: Link equity flows between linked pages.

questions.question: Three blog posts on one site all target the phrase best running shoes, and Google ranks none of them well. What is this self-competition called?
questions.explanation: Keyword cannibalization occurs when multiple pages compete for the same query, splitting ranking signals.

questions.question: A store permanently moves /old-shoes to /shoes and wants ranking equity to transfer. Which redirect status code is correct?
questions.explanation: A 301 redirect signals a permanent move and passes most link equity to the new URL.

questions.question: Google predominantly crawls and ranks the mobile version of a site's pages. What is this indexing model called?
questions.explanation: Mobile-first indexing means Google uses the mobile rendition of content for indexing and ranking.

questions.question: Faceted filters generate dozens of URLs for the same product listing. Which link element consolidates signals to the preferred URL?
questions.explanation: rel="canonical" tells search engines which duplicate URL should receive the consolidated ranking signals.

questions.question: In a Lighthouse audit, which Core Web Vitals metric flags page elements jumping around during load?
questions.explanation: Cumulative Layout Shift measures unexpected layout movement; a good score is under 0.1.
